headline: AI Guard Gateway v0.1.0 mitigates AI endpoint hijacking and prompt injection attacks
summary: This new security reverse proxy protects exposed AI inference APIs like Ollama and LiteLLM from anonymous access and resource abuse.
details: Recent vulnerability analysis revealed a critical risk: exposed AI inference APIs (Ollama, LiteLLM) without security layers allow anonymous access and resource abuse. This poses a significant threat to AI deployments.
In response, AI Guard Gateway v0.1.0 has been developed as a security reverse proxy. It is designed to be deployed in front of any language model to add a crucial layer of protection.

The system was built using the Spec-Driven Development (SDD) methodology. This ensures that every functionality within the gateway responds to verified acceptance criteria, enhancing its reliability and effectiveness.
Beyond implementation, the project underwent a rigorous validation process. This thorough testing confirms its capability to secure AI endpoints against common attack vectors like prompt injection.
caption:
Exposed AI endpoints are vulnerable to hijacking and prompt injection. AI Guard Gateway v0.1.0 offers a new defense.

Recent vulnerability analysis revealed a critical risk: exposed AI inference APIs (Ollama, LiteLLM) without security layers allow anonymous access and resource abuse. This poses a significant threat to AI deployments.

In response, AI Guard Gateway v0.1.0 has been developed as a security reverse proxy. It is designed to be deployed in front of any language model to add a crucial layer of protection.

The system was built using the Spec-Driven Development (SDD) methodology. This ensures that every functionality within the gateway responds to verified acceptance criteria, enhancing its reliability and effectiveness.

Beyond implementation, the project underwent a rigorous validation process. This thorough testing confirms its capability to secure AI endpoints against common attack vectors like prompt injection.

headline: Solon 4.0.3 released with AI loop, modular code talents, and JDK 25 prep
summary: Solon's latest update, v4.0.3, brings a controlled AI loop execution framework, independent code talents, and pre-adaptation for the upcoming JDK 25 LTS release, demonstrating rapid iteration.
details: Solon v4.0.3 was released on July 2, 2026, marking three releases in under a month. This rapid iteration highlights the team's intense focus on AI Agent infrastructure development.

The new solon-ai-loop module provides a controlled loop execution framework for AI agents. It allows agents to iterate until a termination condition is met, working with StopLoopInterceptor for control over max iterations, timeouts, and manual interruption.

Code-related talents, previously bundled in Harness, are now independent in solon-ai-talent-code. This modularization makes Harness leaner and allows code talents to be reused in other contexts, such as the SolonCode CLI.

Solon also pre-adapts for JDK 25, the upcoming LTS release in September 2026. The ScopeLocalJdk25 auto-load mechanism ensures seamless compatibility and leverages JDK 25's scoped value implementation without requiring code changes.
The v4.0.x line offers full LTS guarantees, with minor releases expected roughly every 20 days. Each minor version line will have independent LTS maintenance.

Users on v3.x in production are not rushed to migrate, as v3.10.x is still actively maintained. Migration from v3.x to v4.x primarily affects AI modules and package restructuring, with the core framework remaining largely compatible.
